schema.note: generated aggregate; the register is the store below

recordStore.layout: records/<workstream>/<date>/<recordId>.json (one file per batch record, immutable once its status leaves IN PROGRESS); flags/active.json and flags/resolved.json (the flag register split by status); foundation/<section>.json (meta, tokens, components, standing batch rules and the other non-record sections); indexes/record-index.json and indexes/current-state.json (generated, never hand-edited); design-system-schema.json (generated legacy aggregate).
recordStore.concurrency: Concurrent batches write separate record files and never touch shared files except the generated indexes, which regenerate at commit.
recordStore.backupPolicy: Policy B (record backupPolicyB_2026-09-08, operator decision quoted there): the backup is the immutable record files in git plus milestone tags (scripts/schema/milestone.js) at each workstream close or weekly, whichever comes first; validate-split fails when the latest milestone is older than seven days. No per-batch copy of the aggregate is taken any more; the 90 historical backup files stay as history.
recordStore.howToRecord: An apply-*.js script opens the record with scripts/schema/lib.js openRecord (record gate: the previous record in the workstream must be DONE in indexes/record-index.json); a finalize-*.js script closes it with finalizeRecord; both regenerate the aggregate and indexes. New findings go to flags/active.json through appendFlags; a resolution moves an entry to flags/resolved.json through resolveFlag. Never edit a record file by hand, and never edit a DONE record.
recordStore.readRecord: Find a record by id in indexes/record-index.json and read the file at its path. The last record of a workstream is in indexes/current-state.json byWorkstream.<ws>.latest.

authority.principle: Facts follow evidence. Design decisions stop for the human operator.

library.access: read-only unless the batch is explicitly library work

canonicalClaudeMdSections.note: These CLAUDE.md sections are declared canonical by name rather than copied. CLAUDE.md is digest-checked by the contract, so a change to any of them invalidates the contract.
sections: Where truth lives (precedence: code > Storybook render > production behaviour > Figma)

agentRules.lead: Any agent — Claude, Codex, or other — editing the Figma files or this repo follows the same loop. Work that skips it gets audited and may be superseded.

rules.title: Read before touching
rules.text: Read before touching: CLAUDE.md, then use the validated compact workflow for NPVE work (run node scripts/workflow/validate-workflow.js, read workflow/npve-contract.generated.json, the selected manifest item, and its last record). For other workstreams, or when the compact workflow routes you there, read the record store: indexes/record-index.json, then the record files it names (design-system-schema.json is the aggregate generated from them). The record store remains the authoritative record; the generated contract is a freshness-checked projection; chat history and your own memory are not the record.
rules.note: Amended 2026-09-08 (commit c88ce6c) to route NPVE work through the compact workflow; that amendment had no record until workflowRefactor_closeout_2026-09-08. Amended by schemasplit_phase8_2026-09-08: the register is the append-only record store; the monolith is generated.

rules.title: Audit before building
rules.text: Audit before building: when the current state is uncertain, run a read-only inventory first and report it. Never build onto an unverified state.

rules.title: One batch at a time
rules.text: One batch at a time, with a stop condition stated up front. A batch that grows past its stop condition becomes two batches.

rules.title: Additive only
rules.text: Additive only. Nothing is deleted, and nothing is moved, renamed, or superseded without a record saying so. Archives get a README.

rules.title: No invention
rules.text: No invention. If the library and code lack a pattern, mark it (GAP/DEFECT per the convention) and build with what exists. Recreating a source drawing by hand and calling it a component is a false record, which is worse than the gap.

rules.title: Verify in pixels
rules.text: Verify in pixels. Screenshot what you built and look at it. Property readbacks are claims; renders are evidence. After editing a component, re-screenshot its live instances and diff.

rules.title: Record every batch
rules.text: Record every batch: a dated record file under records/<workstream>/<date>/ via an apply-*.js script (openRecord), findings to flags/active.json (appendFlags). A record is immutable once its status leaves IN PROGRESS. The backup is the committed record files plus a milestone tag (scripts/schema/milestone.js) at each workstream close or weekly, whichever comes first; no per-batch copy of the aggregate. A batch without a record did not happen and will be treated as suspect.
rules.note: Amended by schemasplit_phase8_2026-09-08 (records are files in the append-only store) and by backupPolicyB_2026-09-08 (backup policy B replaces the per-batch full-schema backup; operator decision quoted in that record).

rules.title: Report per rule 13
rules.text: Report per rule 13: full report to disk, short reply, no tables in chat. Change logs in the file are written in plain graphic-design language, not system jargon.

rules.title: Stop on disagreement
rules.text: Resolve unambiguous factual planning mistakes from precedence evidence and record the correction within approved intent. Actual code/library divergence, ambiguous ownership or a new design choice stops for the operator. Do not silently reconcile sources or repeatedly ask permission for routine repairs; follow workflow/execution-policy.md.

rules.title: Record gate
rules.text: Record gate. Before starting any batch, check that the previous batch in this workstream has a schema record. If it does not, refuse the batch and run a read-only state check instead; its record stands in for the missing one.

rules.title: Risk is planner/operator-owned
rules.text: Risk is planner/operator-owned, never executor-owned. Classes are low, medium, high and human-decision as defined in workflow/protocol.json. A manifest tier counts as approved only when the operator's approval is quoted verbatim in the manifest and the record; an unapproved tier lets an item proceed only with per-item operator confirmation, also quoted; a human-decision item does not start until the operator decides. Deterministic gates may compress checks, but every component still gets a comparison render inspected by the executor and shown to the operator.
rules.note: Adopted from amendment 2 of the 2026-09-08 plan review; first written into AGENTS.md by commit c88ce6c as its rule 10, which made AGENTS.md diverge from CLAUDE.md. Numbered 11 in both files from this record on.

recordGate.text: Before starting any batch, check that the previous batch in this workstream has a schema record. If it does not, refuse the batch and run a read-only state check instead; its record stands in for the missing one. In the compact workflow the gate is enforced twice: the apply-*.js script refuses to create the IN PROGRESS record while the previous record is not DONE, and start-batch.js refuses to start while the item's own record is not IN PROGRESS or a dependency is not complete. Since schemasplit_phase8_2026-09-08 the gate reads indexes/record-index.json: openRecord in scripts/schema/lib.js refuses to create a record file while the previous record in the workstream is not DONE there, and start-batch.js refuses while the item's own record file is not IN PROGRESS.

14.title: Change log beside every rebuilt frame
14.text: Every rebuilt frame has a Change log beside it, on its right, listing what changed from the source, from → to, and why in one line, in plain graphic-design language. Rows come from the batch prompt. The change log lives once, as a `_Rebuild comparison/Change log/<screen>` sub-component on Templates holding Change log/Row instances; Row stays a component so styling propagates. The schema remains the record; the change log is its plain-language view.
14.note: Added 2026-09-02; amended the same day to the detached-frame convention (flag npveChangelog_placedLogIsDetached); rewritten 2026-09-04 in repair batch 2 to the instance-swap sub-component convention that stands today.

15.title: Rebuild comparison is the only placement
15.text: Every rebuilt frame sits in a Rebuild comparison on Screens: an instance of the Rebuild comparison master whose three content slots are swapped per screen to `_Rebuild comparison/Reference|Rebuild|Change log/<screen>` sub-components, left to right on a grey backdrop. Each screen and its change log exist exactly once, inside those sub-components; the comparison instance is the only placement, and a fix goes to the sub-component, never to a copy. The reference is a flat export at 2x captioned with its source node id and export date, and does not update when the source changes. The grey backdrop is a deliberate exception to rule 10.
15.note: The 2x reference is produced with the Figma MCP download_assets (source node, png, scale 2) and placed with upload_assets targeting the reference rectangle (method recorded in npveRebuild_comparisonLayout_2026_09_02.transport). Verification proofs are not placements; see proofConvention.

items: Sheets are as tall as their content. The Sidesheet master stays 550 by 600. A placed sheet grows or shrinks to fit its body, and the footer sits right under the last row. Never pad a short sheet to 600 or pin its footer to the bottom.

Helpers under a short sheet are transparent. When a rebuilt sheet is shorter than the comparison slot, the Rebuild sub-component carries no fill, so only the sheet shows white. Nothing false extends below it.

Tall content overflows the slot; the slot does not shrink it. When a reference or a rebuilt sheet is taller than the 600 slot, keep it at 1:1 and switch clipping off on that column of the placed comparison instance. Never scale a reference to fit.
New bodies join the shell through its Body content list. Append the new body component to the Sidesheet's Body content preferred values and leave the default alone. Do not fork the shell.
A new state is a new variant of the body it belongs to. Add State=Empty to the existing body set rather than creating a second set or a loose frame.

Values the library lacks may live in a local NPVE collection. Name the collection NPVE/<kind>, record the operator's decision in the schema, claim no code syntax, and add the value to the library to-do list. Never write it into the library from a consuming file.

proofConvention.text: Verification proofs — instances or frames placed only so a batch can read rendered paint and property state — are named `PROOF — <batch folder> · <what>`, live only through their batch, and are archived under additive-only at batch close: moved unchanged to the Archive page section `06 · Pilot proofs`, listed in the Archive README, never deleted. A proof is not a placement under rule 15 and is never fixed in place; fixes go to the master or sub-component.

executionPolicy.summary: Verify component mappings, build visible milestones, recover from actual state with bounded retries, and preserve a portable execution checkpoint. Resolve routine facts and repairs within scope; ask the UX designer only for real decisions.
executionPolicy.text:
# Reliable execution across models and harnesses

Applies to every executor. Adopted by `workflow_executionReliability_2026-09-10` after the Allergies recovery. Read this once per session; it is also included in the generated contract. This clarifies how to execute approved work, without lowering its risk or replacing the ten standing batch checks.

The execution checkpoint is for Figma build runs. Repository-only work records canvas checks as not applicable; never fabricate component mappings or screenshots to satisfy a documentation batch.

## Talk to the operator as a UX designer

Lead with what changed on the screen. Use familiar design language and show saved screenshots for comparison. Keep code, property names, node IDs, schema details, command transcripts and diagnostic tables in the report unless the operator asks for them or needs a specific setup action. Provide a concise progress update about once a minute during active work: what is now visible, what remains, or the exact obstacle. Never describe an unverified edit as complete.

Planning and execution may happen in one session. The selected model can do both within the operator-approved scope. Do not require Claude, a second chat, a plugin stack, or manual message copying. A change of model or harness is a continuation of the same batch, not permission to restart or duplicate it.

## Establish a buildable plan once

Use the lean startup. Confirm the repository root, target file/page identity and current batch state. Inspect the actual authenticated tool list and make a read-only call against the target. A tool name, seat type or successful identity call does not alone prove canvas write permission. Verify writing through the first intended, authorized edit and its readback; do not create disposable probes solely to test it.

Before building, check the distinct controls needed for the next visible milestone against the actual published components: exact component identity, variant choices, exposed properties and dimensions. Repeated controls can cite the same evidence. Reuse verified mappings from the same session or a current precedent; do not rediscover the whole library. Revalidate a reused mapping if it fails or the library has changed.

Record one short, reusable appearance specification for the composition: card surface, field surface, borders, selected/focused states, and the evidence or approved decision behind them. Link it in `appearance.specification` in new execution checkpoints; do not duplicate it for every field. See `workflow/appearance/npve-edit-forms.md` for the current edit-form requirement. A precedent is reusable only for the properties actually verified: a previously accepted layout is not proof of correct surfaces. Check its linked open findings before reuse.

A transparent library input does not determine the surface of the composed field. Check the enclosing treatment and code/Storybook evidence. Preserve code-first authority: implement the approved appearance using the supported token/composition treatment; if the library cannot express it, report the conflict or GAP instead of silently editing the shared library or inventing an override.

Record the results in the batch's small `execution.json` checkpoint using `workflow/execution-template.json`. Cite saved readback evidence, rather than writing only “verified.” Control evidence uses the native property definitions in a JSON snapshot, as described in `workflow/README.md`; the validator checks the requested properties against it. This supports resumption and the start/finish gates; it is not another approval request or a second batch record. The IN PROGRESS record remains authoritative for scope, decisions and dispositions.

Treat a prompt's component names and estimated dimensions as hypotheses until checked. The Allergies plan called for an outlined 36px Add button; the published white bordered small button was named contained/primary and measured 30px. Resolve an unambiguous factual mistake from code, Storybook and library evidence, document original → correction, and continue within approved intent. Do not invent a missing variant, resize a library control to satisfy an estimate, or repeatedly try an unavailable value. An actual code/library divergence or multiple defensible design choices remains a finding for the operator; do not silently “repair” the library.

## Build visible milestones inside one batch

Use a short sequence such as form → complete sheet → comparison and closeout. A milestone is an internal checkpoint, not a new record or permission boundary. Continue through the authorized batch after it passes.

Make a small group of dependent edits, then check the affected nodes. After a meaningful visual milestone, save and inspect a screenshot before extending it. Check expected text, missing controls, clipping, layout overflow, selected states and default/sample content. Inspect actual instance rendering, not just stored properties or master nodes. Run the required full-page and ten-rule audits at batch completion; repeat broad audits only if subsequent changes invalidate them. The existing concurrency guard still runs before mutations.

At the completed comparison, inspect the whole form, not only the latest repair: card/field surfaces and contrast, borders, labels/content, states, spacing/clipping, and actions. Each material difference from the reference must be corrected or explained by cited code/Storybook evidence and an approved decision where required. Record this brief review at `appearance.review`, with the final screenshot, the inspected areas, and a `differences` list (empty only when no material differences remain). Each difference states the observation, disposition (`corrected` or `approved`), and evidence. A saved image or a passing validator is not visual proof by itself.

If a defect came from a reused pattern, append one tracked finding naming the precedent and known derivatives, with separate review/repair status for each. Link that finding from the appearance specification so the next builder encounters it without a history search. Do not mark all consumers fixed from one corrected screenshot, rewrite DONE records, or expand the current repair to other forms without authorization. Add new consumers when discovered; broad inventory is not required for every batch.

Use documented APIs for the current tool. Load and await the actual fonts before changing text; set instance properties by their exact exposed names; append new nodes to the intended parent immediately; apply fill/hug sizing after fixed resizing. Import and use remote components in the same call. Never swallow an error or assume a generic helper changed a property: read back the affected node and inspect its rendered text. Prefer stable IDs and scoped searches over repeated whole-file scans. One discovery inventory is enough unless new evidence requires another.

## Recover without a retry loop

A failed or disconnected write may still have landed. Read the affected IDs and parent children before any retry. Classify the result as applied, not applied, or still uncertain. If applied, continue from that state; if not applied, make an evidence-based correction; if uncertain, perform read-only diagnosis. Never replay a creation blindly. Server hints such as `safeToRetryWithoutCanvasRead` are not proof of canvas state.

After two unsuccessful attempts at the same operation, stop that operation. Rephrasing the prompt or changing models does not reset this limit. Inspect the exact error and current state once, then use a materially different, evidence-supported approach. Record what changed and verify its result. If no supported correction is available, save the checkpoint and report the specific blocker. Work on independent authorized parts may continue. Do not reinstall servers, switch endpoints, change authentication or add plugins without evidence that the failure is in that layer.

If about five minutes pass without a verified visual change or a concrete diagnostic finding, checkpoint and diagnose the lack of progress instead of accepting another unbounded “Continue.” This is a progress signal, not a total task deadline: slow exports and worthwhile diagnosis can take longer. Do not keep a user waiting through identical retries.

Keep unresolved failures in `execution.json` until readback evidence establishes their resolution. Do not clear them merely to pass a validator. Log failed operation, exact error, known node IDs, whether a mutation landed, and the next different approach in a short batch note. Do not record tokens, credentials, signed asset URLs or guessed tool-call counts.

## Routine repairs and human decisions

Within the approved batch, the executor may correct labels and component properties, clipping and layout mistakes, empty generated placeholders, or a misplaced node it can identify as belonging to this batch. Record moves/conversions/supersession in the IN PROGRESS record **before** performing them, preserving IDs or recording old → new IDs. No second permission is needed for such a repair. Never delete: archive unused batch scaffolding with a README, and do not displace verified or unrelated work. An unrelated leftover does not block a separate, safe part of the form.

Ask the operator only when a real design choice, ownership ambiguity, scope/risk expansion, destructive action or explicit approval boundary remains. Present the visible consequence and a recommendation in plain language. Routine factual corrections are reported, not turned into taste questions. Do not weaken locked risk, oversight or file boundaries to get a gate to pass.

Preserve unrelated dirty files. New runs fingerprint them at startup; finish allows them only if unchanged. Do not hide, relocate, commit or expand the allowlist for unrelated work merely to make a finish gate green. For an older run without a baseline, report that limitation with the completed evidence rather than fabricating a baseline after the fact; it is a workflow limitation, not a reason to rebuild Figma.

## Resume and close

At a handoff, keep the IN PROGRESS record, saved control mappings and this checkpoint. List verified milestone renders, actual created/moved IDs, unresolved errors, and exactly one next action. Resume by checking those IDs once. Do not reread every historical record, rebuild a completed milestone, or retest authentication just because the model changed.

At close, every planned milestone must have a saved render inspected by the executor, all unresolved failures must have a recorded resolution, and all existing standing checks still apply. Show the comparison to the operator, save the report, finalize and commit. Record operator acceptance in the next appropriate record without editing a DONE record. A screenshot checkpoint does not silently grant approval for the next batch.

## What the local checks can and cannot guarantee

New workflow runs require `execution.json` at start, validate it before mutations, and require verified milestone renders at finish. The checker rejects missing mappings/evidence, unresolved failures and incomplete milestones. Historical runs are not retroactively invalidated. It checks the submitted evidence and local files; it cannot independently authenticate Figma, inspect pixels, count unreported retries or force a harness to call it. The executor must follow this policy honestly. Evaluate cheaper models on a clean bounded task by visible progress, corrections and total cost/time, not token price alone.

operatingLoop: Validate this contract before reading it as current truth.
Record gate: confirm the previous batch in the workstream has a DONE record in indexes/record-index.json; if not, refuse and run a read-only state check whose record stands in.
Use the manifest item selected by the planner; the executor may not change its risk class. An unapproved tier needs per-item operator confirmation, quoted verbatim.
Verify file identity and current live state before writes.
Declare one bounded batch and stop condition.
Open the IN PROGRESS record as a new file under records/ (apply-*.js via openRecord) before Figma mutation, regenerate this contract, then start the batch guard.

Verify the next milestone mappings and save execution.json before start. Mutate sequentially, verify visible milestones, and use bounded evidence-based recovery; stop the failed operation before extending dependent work.
Run deterministic checks and inspect at least one comparison render per component.
Save the comparison render and full report; show the render to the operator.

Archive the batch proofs per proofConvention, finalize the record (finalize-*.js via finalizeRecord), regenerate this contract, pass the finish gate, and commit with an explicit allowlist. At a workstream close, or when a week has passed since the last milestone, create a milestone tag on the committed tree.

nonNegotiables.recordsImmutable: A record file is never edited once its status leaves IN PROGRESS; a later batch that must annotate an earlier record writes the annotation in its own record.
nonNegotiables.riskPlannerOwned: Tiers are approved by the operator with a verbatim quote; executors never assign or lower them.

standingBatchRules._purpose: Non-negotiable checks every future batch runs before reporting. Added after the paint-opacity defect reached four already-signed-off components.
standingBatchRules.1_instancePaintVerification: Place ONE INSTANCE of every new variant and read its RENDERED paints — colour, effective alpha and bound variable — comparing each against its master. Master-level reads are NOT evidence: paint-level opacity renders correctly on a master and incorrectly on an instance, which is exactly how the defect survived four batches. Any alpha must live in the variable's stored rgba, never as paint-level opacity. SCOPE: that last sentence governs UNBOUND paints only - for a BOUND paint Figma surfaces the variable's stored alpha into paint.opacity, and that mirrored value is correct; read rule 9_boundPaintAlpha before touching it.
standingBatchRules.2_unboundPaintAudit: Walk EVERY top-level node on EVERY page, not just component sets. Reference frames, notes frames and loose glyphs count. Auditing only component sets is what let 3 unbound paints sit in the Radio reference frame across several batches.
standingBatchRules.3_referenceCounts: Count componentPropertyReferences per variant after any clone or combineAsVariants — cloning a variant inside a set silently drops them all.
standingBatchRules.4_skipInvisibleFalse: Set figma.skipInvisibleInstanceChildren = false before any audit walk, so boolean-hidden slots are inspected.
standingBatchRules.5_opacityLast: If paint-level opacity is genuinely unavoidable somewhere, apply it as the final operation AND verify on an instance. Prefer promoting to a computed variable.
standingBatchRules.6_enumerateDontRecall: When remediating or sweeping, enumerate from the file rather than from a previously reported list. The alpha remediation's known list was missing 18 of 48 paints.
standingBatchRules.7_fileIdentityFirst: Every Figma call passes fileKey YX2n4YLrEpBXNbcc73T6dw explicitly — never rely on an ambient or last-used file. Every session's FIRST Figma action verifies file identity against this schema's page inventory (figmaBuild.pages._order) before any read informs a decision or any write occurs; if the page list does not match, stop and report rather than proceeding. Added 2026-08-03 after a session read the legacy team library (ZPf0sJy83aPyrHjCVHomya, 'Tebra Working UI Kit') and produced a full reorganisation analysis against the wrong file. Note that figma.root.name returns 'Document' for both files, so the file NAME is not a usable identity check — the page list is.
standingBatchRules.8_roundWithRecord: Never carry a fractional dimension into Figma. Two cases, one treatment. (a) pxToRem inflation, where an intended integer exists behind the fraction: bind the intended integer, record computedPx. (b) Authored-fractional sources, where no intended integer exists — a fractional spacing multiplier, a viewBox ratio, a non-square viewBox in a square box: ROUND to the nearest integer and record the true value as computedPx in both the component description and the schema, and label the rounding a design decision with its source and date. Added 2026-08-03 when the primary nav produced the first case-(b) values (76.8, 44.8, 23.88, 18.24); Daniel ruled round-with-record as design authority. Intrinsic geometry is out of scope for this rule: VECTOR and GROUP bounds are the union of their path data, are not authored, and are not rounded — the tier 6 illustrations already set that precedent.
standingBatchRules.9_boundPaintAlpha: Before changing ANY paint-level opacity, first check whether that paint has a bound colour variable. If it does, Figma SURFACES the variable's stored alpha into paint.opacity - it does NOT multiply the two. A paint bound to a variable storing rgba(0,0,0,0.87) correctly reads back paint.opacity 0.87 and renders at 0.87; that is the expected state, not a double-alpha defect, and it must be left alone. Forcing such a paint to opacity 1 DISCARDS the alpha and renders the node fully opaque. Rule 1's 'never as paint-level opacity' applies to UNBOUND paints only. Established empirically 2026-08-26 (checkboxFlushHaloFix2026_08_26d.alphaFindingThatOverturnsAnEarlierEntry) after the opposite assumption produced a real regression on Alert filled/warning; reverted and audited library-wide 2026-08-27 (boundAlphaRegressionRevert2026_08_27). To re-confirm at any time: bind a rectangle to an alpha-carrying variable, never set opacity, then read paint.opacity back - it returns the variable's alpha.
standingBatchRules.10_cloneDropsPropertyRefs: Cloning a variant to add a new axis value DROPS componentPropertyReferences on every child. The clone keeps its layers and looks correct, but Label/icon-visibility/icon-swap stop responding — instance property values are stored yet never render, so a swapped instance silently shows the component default. After any variant clone, re-apply refs by copying them from a known-good sibling keyed on child layer name, then verify by reading a nested instance rendered characters against its property value, not just the property value. Hit during buttonInheritColour2026_08_28.

openFlags.summary: The patient header band (1397x96, two rows, Restricted text button) repeats identically on all 27 encounter frames; the library has none, the Proposals file holds a v1 composition at 900x72 (built 2026-08-19).

The top nav on every encounter frame is a Kit Primary Nav; the library Nav/Bar family exists but its home is unresolved (navComponentsOnCompositionsPage OPEN), so a library-consuming page shell cannot start with it.

Sheets sit on the page two ways: inline as the 450/550-wide left column, and as right-docked full-height overlays (550 and 483 wide, square corners, no scrim). Our Sidesheet Placement=Docked right has 8/0/0/8 corners and one width.
The Rebuild comparison master (1708 wide, 550 slots) cannot hold a 1429-wide reference beside a 1429-wide rebuild with a change log.
The encounter page body is #FBF9F8 on every frame; the library has no such token and the coded default canvas is beige #E8E5DF (beigeSurfaceInvestigation2026_08_31).
Module Dropdown instances are parked at x -437 outside four encounter frames and one hidden loose instance sits at page level; mockup artefacts, not a page convention.
The Patient header (proposal geometry) needs 10px vertical padding; Tebra/Dimension has no space/10, so the value is a literal.
Library Split button exposes only Size and State; its label ("New Note") and leading plus are fixed nested content, so consumers override nested text and hide the plus by instance override.
Badge variant=dot anchors an 8px dot to the top-right of a 24px child; an inline status dot before text is not expressible, so the note header carries a drawn 8px ellipse bound to color/success/main.
The Modules pill uses Icon/Menu and Icon/PlusOutlined on a library Button (pill, 122x38); the source is a white r8 144x40 pill with a Material widgets glyph.

The Health Status/Observations helpers are named "Rebuild helper · Health Status/Observations" and "Reference helper · Health Status/Observations" instead of the _Rebuild comparison/<Reference|Rebuild>/<screen> pattern that every other comparison uses.
The toolbar needs mic, transcribe, person-heart and template-list glyphs the library lacks; Icon/Telehealth, Icon/UserOutlined and Icon/List stand in, the transcribe pill state is unbuilt.

Nothing in the library expresses an inline status toggle (radio dot + bold teal label); built minimal as a local Transcription status/Start piece from Icon/RadioChecked (MUI) and an h5 text, per audit invention row 15.
No vitals, lab, allergy or timeline glyph in the library; the five new module chips use Icon/Clinical, Icon/UserGroupFilled, Icon/Reports, Icon/AttentionOutlined and Icon/Calendar.

Icon/Clinical and Icon/Reports carry a vector fill bound color/common/white, so they vanish on light surfaces; the shell batch's Problems chip had shown a white glyph on pale teal. Chips 2, 4 and 6 now bind the glyph fill to color/text/primary as an instance override.
Toolbar pills are the library Button medium (38 tall, primary stroke, Akkurat 14) where the mockup draws 42-tall pills with a #8CA7A2 stroke; library wins, logged in the change log.
The Split button instance 424:4417 in the Note card footer is hidden and renamed SUPERSEDED rather than deleted (rule 1); its nested segments cannot be un-exposed by the API.

A loose FRAME named "Module chip" (488:8725, 116x40, teal fill, inner frame + Icon/Close instance) sits at (485,1524) in Templates 15 · Encounter page shell beside the Module chip set 426:4213; no record or flag cites it.
